document.about: NIST/AAPS interlaboratory study, SEC protocol (31 August 2023). Six pages from a word processor: tables whose rows are drawn but not ruled, a table split across a page break, conditions per antibody with units in the headers.

notes: 2026-11-17: the troubleshooting table's part on page 6 opens with an empty cell, so its text starts with a tab, and its nif:isString had the tab trimmed. A consumer comparing each element's string with its slice refused the document. The offsets check covers it.

checks.issue: Table 1 sets each protein and its formulation once, centred across three sample rows the ruling does not separate. The wrapped formulation was split into rows (`pH` / `5.0`) and the protein sat on the middle sample only.
The second formulation's first two lines sit on the samples' baselines, a row apart, the second carrying on the first.

row.Formulations: 12.5 mM L-histidine, 12.5 mMol L-histidine HCl, pH 6.0

checks.issue: Read well from the start: each antibody's conditions on its row, units in the column headers. Guarded so it stays so.
The second antibody's conditions on its own row.
Table 3 runs from page 5 onto page 6 with no repeated header. The part on page 6 was read as its own table, its first rows taken for a three-row header.

row.Probable Cause: Column shedding or sample adsorption on the column

checks.issue: A problem that starts on page 6 keeps its own causes.

row.Probable Cause: Excessive tubing length or tubing I.D. too large
row.Resolution: Reduce tubing length and use recommended tubing I.D.

checks.issue: A data row of the continued table named the columns of every cell below it.
